site_ui.lead: Practitioners show how a cell site rent stream that typically sells for 16 to 17.5 times annual rent can swing by hundreds of thousands of dollars on right of first refusal, escalator, easement and carrier fine print.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies on cell tower leases, billboards and industrial outdoor storage. Every claim, metric and quote carries timestamped inline attribution to the practitioner channel and video it came from.

flow: Name every carrier on the site from meter labels, equipment cabinets and building permits, flag Dish exposure, and walk away from single-tenant sites.
Check the lease for right of first refusal, confidentiality, consent-to-assign, defined premises and owner relocation rights before soliciting any offer.
Pull title and confirm rent is still flowing, because even a paid attorney-title review can miss a previously sold easement.
Price the stream as a multiple of annual rent, compare buyer discount rates of 8 to 12% against owner-side 4 to 6%, and stress-test rent stopping in year five to eight.
Demand written letters of intent and sample easement documents from every buyer, since a handful of money sources sit behind roughly 20 buyout brands and clawbacks surface only on paper.
Push for revenue share, escalators of at least 3% and ROFR removal, keep renewals short, and split the lump sum across December and January to spread the tax.
